reconstruction.scope: Dated 2010 surviving Temple of Baalshamin: roofless rectangular ashlar cella, six free-standing Corinthian porch shafts with projecting brackets, open side windows with pedimented surrounds and attached pilasters, tall gated doorway, continuous surviving upper stone beams/cornice, low stepped podium and a small selection of fallen stone/drum fragments. This is the photographed pre-destruction ruin, not a reconstruction of its complete ancient roof or today’s damaged remains.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Human-scaled ordinary 2010 pictures guide a roughly7.8m surviving wall/capital elevation and8.5m cornice above the stepped podium. Shaft proportions, brackets, window pediments, ashlar courses, broken edges and scattered fragment inventory are medium-fi estimates. No original roof/pediment, full courtyard colonnade, fine inscriptions, sculpture or navigable interior is reconstructed.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Reuse pinned standard temple_of_bel Palmyra PMTiles/Mapzen data. The small podium floor is above the maximum nearby native grade, with a buried base and shallow front treads. Preserve native terrain/water without cutouts. Current DEM/map context is explicitly an approximate setting for a dated historical exterior, not a reconstructed 2010 streetscape or surveyed archaeological pavement.
